title: Keeping the balance
objectives: Solve one-step equations by doing the same thing to both sides
Choose the inverse operation that undoes what was done to the unknown

screens.title: Keeping the balance
screens.prose: A scale holds blocks we can read and one mystery block, $x$. We will find what $x$ weighs without ever letting the scale tip.
The scale is level. On the left sit the mystery block $x$ and a 5. On the right sits a 12. Type an amount, then tap Take away.
screens.question: Leave $x$ alone on one pan, with the beam still level.

hints.text: What sits beside $x$ on the left pan?
Only the 5 block is in the way of $x$.
Take away 5 from both pans. The 12 on the right becomes 7.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take away exactly what sits beside $x$, from both pans.

byKey.unsolved: The beam is level, but $x$ still has company. Take away the rest of what sits beside it.

explain.text: You took 5 off both pans, so the beam never moved. What is left says $x = 7$. Check: $7 + 5 = 12$.

screens.prose: We write a level scale as an **equation**. Here $3x = 21$: three $x$ blocks balance 21. Finding $x$ is called **solving** the equation.
screens.question: Solve $3x = 21$ on the scale: leave one $x$ alone, with the beam level.

hints.text: Taking weight away cannot help: nothing sits beside the $x$ blocks.
Three equal blocks. Split each pan into three equal parts.
Divide both by 3. Each pan keeps a third: one $x$ against 7.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Split both pans into the same number of equal parts.

byKey.unsolved: The beam is level, but more than one $x$ is left. Divide both pans by the number of $x$ blocks.

explain.text: You split both pans into three equal parts and kept one part of each. Each part still balances, so $x = 7$. Check: $3 \times 7 = 21$.

screens.prose: Now four $x$ blocks balance 6. The answer does not have to be a whole number.
screens.question: Solve $4x = 6$ on the scale.

hints.text: How many $x$ blocks are there? Split both pans into that many parts.
The 6 has to be shared between four $x$ blocks.
Divide both by 4, or halve both twice. $6 \div 4 = 1.5$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Keep splitting both pans equally until one $x$ is left.

byKey.unsolved: Some $x$ blocks are still together. Keep splitting both pans until one $x$ is left.

explain.text: Dividing both pans by 4 leaves one $x$ against $6 \div 4 = 1.5$. Halving twice does the same: 6, then 3, then 1.5. Check: $4 \times 1.5 = 6$.

screens.prose: A new scale: $x + 4 = 10$. This time you can also tap a single block to lift it off its own pan.
screens.question: Leave $x$ alone on one pan, with the beam level.

hints.text: What happens to the beam when only one pan gets lighter?
Whatever leaves the left pan must leave the right pan too.
Use Take away 4 from both. Then $x$ balances 6.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Keep the beam level while you leave $x$ alone.

byKey.unbalanced: You lifted a block off one pan only, and the beam tipped. $x$ alone is lighter than 10, so $x = 10$ is false.
byKey.unsolved: Level, but $x$ is not alone yet. Take the 4 away from both pans.

explain.text: Lifting the 4 off the left alone tips the scale, so it cannot claim $x = 10$. Taking 4 from both keeps it level: $x = 6$. Check: $6 + 4 = 10$.

screens.prose: A minus sign will not fit on a scale, so use a number line. Here $x - 3 = 8$: start at $x$, go 3 to the left, and you land on 8.
screens.question: Drag $x$ to the number it must be.

hints.text: $x - 3$ is 3 less than $x$. So is $x$ to the left or the right of 8?
Start at 8 and undo the 3 that was taken away.
Go back up 3 from 8 to reach 11. Check: $11 - 3 = 8$.

byKey.subtracted: You went 3 to the left of 8. But 8 is already 3 below $x$, so $x$ sits 3 above 8.

explain.text: Undoing a subtraction means adding: $x = 8 + 3 = 11$. On a scale you would add 3 to both pans. The arrow shows $11 - 3$ landing on 8.

screens.prose: Here $x$ is cut into 4 equal parts, and one part is 5: $\dfrac{x}{4} = 5$. Tap a step to do it to both sides. Undo takes a step back.
screens.question: Solve $\dfrac{x}{4} = 5$.

ops.label: Divide both sides by 4
ops.why: You divided again, which cuts $x$ into smaller parts. $x$ was divided by 4, so multiply by 4 to undo it.

ops.label: Subtract 4 from both sides
ops.why: Nothing was added to $x$, so there is nothing to subtract. The 4 divides $x$.

hints.text: What was done to $x$? Do the opposite to both sides.
One quarter of $x$ is 5. All four quarters make $x$.
Multiply both sides by 4: $x = 20$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Undo the division with its opposite, on both sides.

explain.text: You multiplied both sides by 4, the opposite of dividing by 4. So $x = 4 \times 5 = 20$. Check: $20 \div 4 = 5$.

screens.prose:
Each time, you did the **inverse operation** to both sides: the opposite of what had been done to $x$.

$$x + a = b \;\Rightarrow\; x = b - a \qquad ax = b \;\Rightarrow\; x = \dfrac{b}{a}$$

$$x - a = b \;\Rightarrow\; x = b + a \qquad \dfrac{x}{a} = b \;\Rightarrow\; x = ab$$
screens.question: Which single move solves $x - 7.5 = 12$?

options.why: You repeated the operation already there. That gives $x - 15 = 4.5$, further from $x$ alone.

options.text: Add 7.5 to the left side only
options.why: Changing one side only tips the scale. The right side must gain 7.5 too.
$x$ was not multiplied by 7.5. The 7.5 was taken away, so add it back.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Undo the subtraction, on both sides.

explain.text: Adding 7.5 to both sides undoes the subtraction and keeps the balance. So $x = 19.5$. Check: $19.5 - 7.5 = 12$.

screens.prose: You hold 40 shares of one stock. Your broker says the position is worth £1,286.00. Call the share price $p$, so $40p = 1286$.
screens.question: What is the share price, in pounds?

hints.text: What is done to $p$ to make 1,286?
The value is 40 lots of $p$. Undo the multiplication.
Divide both sides by 40: $p = 1286 \div 40$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide both sides of $40p = 1286$ by 40.

byKey.times: You multiplied by 40. The value is already 40 times the price, so divide.
byKey.minus: You took 40 away. $40p$ means 40 times $p$, so divide by 40.
byKey.flipped: You divided 40 by 1,286. The price is the value shared out over 40 shares.

explain.text: Dividing both sides by 40 undoes the multiplication: $p = 32.15$. Check: $40 \times 32.15 = 1286$. The price comes out to the penny exactly.

ideas: An equation is a level scale. Doing the same thing to both sides keeps it level.
Undo what was done to $x$ with the inverse operation: add to undo subtracting, divide to undo multiplying.
Check a solution by putting it back in: $7 + 5 = 12$ confirms $x = 7$.

formula.name: Keeping the balance
formula.tex: a = b \;\Rightarrow\; a + c = b + c, \quad a - c = b - c, \quad ac = bc, \quad \dfrac{a}{c} = \dfrac{b}{c}
formula.note: Divide only by a number that is not zero.

summary.trap: Taking the 4 off the left pan only tips the scale. $x + 4 = 10$ gives $x = 6$, not $x = 10$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Subtract 2.75 from both sides.

byKey.added: You added 2.75. It was added to $x$, so subtract it from both sides.

explain.text: Subtracting 2.75 from both sides leaves $x = 6.35$. Check: $6.35 + 2.75 = 9.1$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide both sides by 6.

byKey.multiplied: You multiplied by 6. $6x$ is already 6 times $x$, so divide.
byKey.subtracted: You took 6 away. $6x$ means 6 times $x$, so divide by 6.
byKey.flipped: You divided 6 by 27. Share the 27 between 6 instead.

explain.text: Dividing both sides by 6 gives $x = 4.5$. Check: $6 \times 4.5 = 27$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply both sides by 3.

byKey.divided: You divided by 3 again. $x$ was divided by 3, so multiply to undo it.

explain.text: Multiplying both sides by 3 undoes the division: $x = 12.6$. Check: $12.6 \div 3 = 4.2$.

options.text: Took 8 off the left side but not the right

options.why: Taking 8 off both sides gives $x = 12$, not 20.
That gives $x + 16 = 28$. Mo's line has no 16 or 28.

feedback.correct: Mo changed one side only, so the balance tipped.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare Mo's line with $x + 8 = 20$.

explain.text: Mo removed the 8 from the left and left the right at 20. The sides no longer match, so $x = 20$ is false. Taking 8 from both gives $x = 12$.
